verses.author: model_A
verses.text: An orchard planted by a man who never tasted its fruit.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the grafted branch remembers
a taste it never had

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
spring rain still finds
the roots that were told
they belonged to another tree

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
we drink from wells
our grandmothers dug blind,
never asking whose thirst it was

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the water tastes of iron
and someone else's patience

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a bucket left rusting
still holds the shape
of every hand that gripped it

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the well goes dry some summers
but the hands keep coming back
just to remember how to hold

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the shape of holding
outlasts the water --
we teach our children the grip, not the thirst

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
small palms learn the curve
before they learn the word for empty --
this too is a kind of drinking

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the curve stays in the hand
long after the mouth forgets
what it was reaching for

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the fingers keep reaching anyway --
old habit mistaken for hunger,
hunger mistaken for love

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
love mistaken for a cup we keep
setting on the table --
someone always coming home thirsty

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the table worn smooth
where thirst has sat so many years --
we call that scar a welcome

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the door left unlocked
so the scar can keep arriving --
we sweep the same step twice

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
dust rises where the broom bends --
even emptiness leaves footprints
we mistake for someone staying

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the footprints fade by morning --
still we set out shoes by the door
in case the emptiness wants company
